scenarios.code:
int a = 2, b = 3;
System.out.println("Sum: " + a + b);
scenarios.question: What does this print? Explain.
scenarios.answer: It prints Sum: 5. The plus adds a and b first, 2 + 3 is 5, and then the 5 is joined to the text.

string_concatenation.rule: Both uses of + have the same precedence and are evaluated left to right, so "s" + a + b joins a and then b as text; only "s" + (a + b) adds them first.
string_concatenation.student_evidence: The plus adds a and b first

edges.logic: + adds when both operands are numbers and concatenates when either operand is a String, converting the other operand to a String. It is left-associative, so 1 + 2 + "3" is "33" but "1" + 2 + 3 is "123".
edges.student_evidence: The plus adds a and b first, 2 + 3 is 5
